archetype: A five-colour legendary toolbox built around one repeatable battlefield tutor, closed by a checker-passed unbounded combat loop (stack 002, Najeela + Derevi). deck-audit reports 'archetype unestablished (none — base targets apply)', so the frame does NOT agree: no archetype override was applied and every target below is the base template. That matters most for threat-density and creatures, where a combo-toolbox and a creature deck want different numbers.
verdict: It functions and it converts: 0.935 turn-3 land-drop rate, commander cast on a mean turn of 2.963, and a rules-verified unbounded kill already in the 99. What limits it is a cost, not a card. FIVE cards in the 99 carry the string {W}{U}{B}{R}{G}. I matched three fields across every entry in cards.json — mana_cost, oracle_text and each face of card_faces — because Esika, God of the Tree // The Prismatic Bridge has an EMPTY top-level mana_cost and carries the string on card_faces[1]. Four of the five SPEND it: Sisay's activation, Najeela's activation, Jodah, the Unifier's printed cast cost, and The Prismatic Bridge's cast cost. Exactly one PRODUCES it: Jegantha, the Wellspring. Every other route to that five-pip, zero-generic bill is board-conditional, enumerated card by card in the engine block — and it is the bill the deck cannot count on paying twice in a turn cycle.

engine.declared: Sisay's {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} activation puts a legendary permanent with mana value below her power onto the battlefield, each fetch adding colours that raise her power and widen the next fetch, until the ladder reaches Najeela and the combat loop.

components.reading: Declared as the five-colour battery, and only one member is one. Read from cards.json oracle text: Jegantha adds {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} off one tap regardless of board; Bloom Tender and Faeburrow Elder add one mana per colour among permanents you control (beside Sisay alone that is {W}{G}); Esika adds one mana of any colour and grants the same ability to OTHER legendary creatures; Relic of Legends adds one per activation, tapping a legend; Selvala adds X in any combination where X is the greatest power among your creatures and costs {G} to fire. So 67.9% is the rate at which one of six cards is drawn, not the rate at which the deck can pay the bill.

The thinnest declared group and the one under-declared: it is four cards at a 25.8% opener, but the FUNCTION — raise Sisay's power so the fetch is worth making — is also served by Flowering of the White Tree (+2/+1 to legendary creatures, mana value 2 and itself fetchable) and by five counter sources (Bristly Bill, Mikaeus, Katilda, Shalai, Heliod). Treat 52.5% as a floor on the wrong set.

Seven cards, 74.7% assembled, mean turn 2.836 — this is why the commander lands on turn 2.963. Note that Sol Ring and Delighted Halfling accelerate toward Sisay without being able to pay one pip of what she then does.
Eleven cards, 88.4% assembled, mean turn 2.3 — the deck is holding an answer for its commander in 88.4% of games. This part is finished.

single_points_of_failure.why: FIVE cards in the 99 carry the string {W}{U}{B}{R}{G}, matched over mana_cost, oracle_text and every face of card_faces in cards.json. Four spend it — Sisay's activation, Najeela's activation, Jodah, the Unifier's cast cost, and The Prismatic Bridge's cast cost on card_faces[1] of Esika, God of the Tree // The Prismatic Bridge, whose top-level mana_cost is the empty string. One produces it: Jegantha, the Wellspring, {4}{R/G}, fetchable only at Sisay power 6, and the only permanent here that adds all five colours from a single activation REGARDLESS of board. The other five members of this component all reach the conjunction, and every one of them needs a board first: Bloom Tender and Faeburrow Elder tap once for one mana of each colour among permanents you control, so they are the whole bill only after the board already shows five colours; Selvala, Heart of the Wilds pays it in one activation for {G} and a tap once any creature has power 5 (bracket_report lists Najeela + Selvala as one of the deck's four two-card infinites); Relic of Legends' second ability carries no tap symbol on Relic, so it fires once per untapped legendary creature you control; Esika grants '{T}: Add one mana of any color' to OTHER legendary creatures, one mana per body. Against a goldfished 5.869 mean available mana at turn 6, none of that is a second activation you can count on — one, and the turn is gone.

lean_into.what: Fetch Flowering of the White Tree before you fetch a body.
lean_into.why: It is a legendary enchantment at mana value 2, so Sisay reaches it at power 3 — one colour among other legendary permanents. It then gives her +2/+1, two ladder rungs bought with no new colour, plus ward {1} on the creature the whole deck routes through. It is not the only mana-value-2-or-less fetch that takes her 3 → 5: on a mono-white board Kinnan, Bonder Prodigy ({G}{U}, two new colours) does it too, and on a mono-blue board Katilda, Lotho and Saffi each do. What is true of Flowering alone, across all ten legal targets at that power, is that its gain is board-INDEPENDENT — +2 on every board and +3 on a board with no white — while every other target's gain is a colour count and nothing else: it adds power only for a colour not already among her other legendary permanents, and Mox Amber, being colourless, never adds one.

cut_candidates.why: It is counted on three axes at once — threat-density, protection and interaction — and it is the weakest entry on each. Four damage against 120 opposing life is not a finisher, and the indestructible mode is the third-best protection spell in a deck holding Flawless Maneuver (free while the commander is out) and Heroic Intervention (hexproof as well as indestructible, and hexproof is what beats the targeted removal that actually kills Sisay).
cut_candidates.cost_of_cutting: Three axes move, not two, and each falls by one wherever the deck stands: interaction 8 → 7 (under the Walser floor of 8 this entry cites), protection 7 → 6 (inside the 5-7 band, so nothing downstream breaks) and threat-density 3 → 2 (under Zupke's cited floor of at least 3 finishers). The previous pass said Beast Within covered the interaction loss; run over the whole swap set it does not, and that claim is withdrawn. Beast Within's one removal:spot is already spent covering the An Offer You Can't Refuse cut, so the three prescribed swaps end at interaction 8 / protection 7 / threat-density 3, while pairing Beast Within with Boros Charm instead ends at 7 / 6 / 2 — two floors broken rather than none. Walking Ballista, which the previous pass paired here, carries buff:counters / removal:damage / threat:body and no wincon role, so it moves threat-density by zero. Boros Charm is also the only card in the 99 that grants double strike — Samut has it natively, nothing else hands it out. So this cut is HELD: make it only inside a swap whose add carries a wincon role AND a removal or counterspell role, and this diagnosis names no such card.

open_questions.question: Does Zupke's 'at least 3 finishers' floor bind a deck whose only assertable kill is a checker-passed unbounded combat loop, and whose three counted finishers this diagnosis calls filler?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is what holds Boros Charm in the 99. Cutting it moves three axes down by one — interaction 8 → 7, protection 7 → 6, threat-density 3 → 2 — and only protection stays inside its band. threat-density counts wincon:alt, wincon:drain and wincon:combat, and no card this diagnosis names restores it. The answer decides whether the weakest card in the deck is allowed to leave, and what its replacement has to do.

open_questions.question: With Human chosen, does Secluded Courtyard's mana pay Sisay's {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} activation cost? Its clause reads 'or activate an ability of a creature source of the chosen type', and Sisay is a Human Soldier while Najeela is a Human Warrior.
open_questions.why_it_matters: mana_analysis scores Secluded Courtyard as producing nothing, so if it pays the activation every colour count in the colour-sources axis is a floor by one land. Plaza of Heroes is NOT part of this question and is already settled: its third mode, '{T}: Add one mana of any color among legendary permanents you control', carries no spend restriction, and the deck's own checker-passed stack 002 pays an identical {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} activation cost with it.

open_questions.question: Re-declare goldfish_targets.json's 'three-colour legend to grow her' group to include the cards that raise Sisay's power without adding a colour — Flowering of the White Tree, Bristly Bill, Mikaeus, Katilda, Shalai, Heliod — and re-run.
open_questions.why_it_matters: The audit calls this the thinnest component at 4 cards and 52.5%, and the prescription for a thinnest component is usually 'add redundancy'. If the real group is ten cards the deck does not need that slot, and a card would be added for nothing.

open_questions.question: Stacks 001 (can Sisay activate the turn she lands, and what may she fetch) and 003 (may a freshly fetched legend be tapped for Relic of Legends, and may it use Esika's granted ability) both carry checker.verdict 'fail'.
open_questions.why_it_matters: Both questions decide whether the deck chains two fetches in one turn or across two, which is the difference between the loop assembling on turn 6 and on turn 8. Nothing in this diagnosis rests on either, and nothing can until they pass.

open_questions.question: strategy.md has no section on toolbox construction or on treating library ACCESS as the resource a deck spends.
open_questions.why_it_matters: redundancy-vs-tutors models a tutor as card selection — k tutors act like k+1 copies of every card — which is the wrong model for a free, repeatable, battlefield tutor. Every judgment here about how many one-of answers Sisay justifies is ungrounded for that reason.

gaps: No data/decks/sisay/deck_recon.json (deck-audit freshness reports recon absent), so nothing here is weighed against per-commander inclusion rates. Every add is grounded in this deck's artifacts, not in what strong Sisay lists run. A deck-recon pass in MODE recon would settle it.

No candidate_pool.json for this deck, so the three adds come from upgrade-facts' pool channels and a direct cards.csv legality check rather than a scored pool. Legality, colour identity and not-already-in-the-99 were verified for all three; fit was not scored.

The audit ran with no archetype established, so base targets applied to threat-density, creatures and interaction. A combo-toolbox at bracket 4 plausibly wants different numbers on all three, and the diagnosis says so rather than pretending the base target is a verdict.

Nine of the ten contained combo lines are unverified. Only stack 002 (Najeela + Derevi) has checker.verdict 'pass', and its own final_state calls the pair 'not a self-contained two-card infinite'. Every other line in this document is named, never asserted.

The claim that Chromatic Lantern and Cryptolith Rite let the deck pay {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} twice in a turn cycle is arithmetic over the goldfish's mean available mana, not a simulated result — the goldfish models resource development, not activations. A goldfish target declaring 'two Sisay activations in one turn' would measure it.

threat-density is the one axis this prescription cannot improve. It measures exactly 3, this document's own reading calls all three counted cards filler, and none of the three adds carries a wincon role — Chromatic Lantern and Cryptolith Rite are ramp:rock / utility:activated, Beast Within is removal:spot / threat:tokens. Walking Ballista, proposed in the previous pass and withdrawn here, is buff:counters / removal:damage / threat:body and moves the axis by zero; I ran the count with and without it. Naming a finisher this deck actually wants needs a candidate_pool.json or a deck-recon pass, and this diagnosis has neither.

findings.note: Chromatic Lantern is labelled `closes: "colour-sources"` and its `why` says the deck has "21 black sources against a 36 target; this makes all 40 a source of every colour". I recomputed mana_analysis's source counting (manabase.count_sources + land_colors, plus mana_analysis.nonland_producer_kind) over the deck and reproduced the tracked file EXACTLY (lands W15/U12/B12/R12/G14, nonland W11/U10/B9/R9/G13, total W26/U22/B21/R21/G27). Applying all three prescribed swaps the totals become W27/U23/B22/R22/G28 against unchanged targets B36/others22, so the colour-sources axis moves from -15 to -14 and STILL READS UNDER. The reason is that manabase.land_colors is per-card and models no static grant, so Lantern's 'Lands you control have "{T}: Add one mana of any color"' is invisible to the measure; Lantern and Cryptolith Rite each score as one any-colour rock (+2 per colour) and cutting An Offer You Can't Refuse removes one (-1), for a net +1. The card is correct, in identity, Commander-legal (cards.csv legal_commander == legal) and its mechanism is described accurately — the defect is that the entry names an axis the add will not close and supplies no post-swap figure, while the neighbouring add_candidates[2] supplies an exact one (`axis_after_swap`). It is also in tension with the document's own axes[3], which argues the -15 headline is one card (Dauthi Voidwalker) and that 21 sources is fine for the single {B} the deck actually needs — yet `evidence.axis_gap` leans on that same shortfall. The honest label is the one used for Cryptolith Rite: `engine component: five-colour mana source`, which is also where both single_points_of_failure entries already list it as a closer.

The Kodama of the West Tree entry prices the cut as "the deck loses its only way to find a basic land". Read against cards.json, that superlative fails on its own membership: the deck runs NINE fetchlands (Arid Mesa, Flooded Strand, Marsh Flats, Misty Rainforest, Polluted Delta, Scalding Tarn, Verdant Catacombs, Windswept Heath, Wooded Foothills), each reading 'Search your library for a <type> or <type> card', and all six basic copies (Forest, Island, Mountain, Plains x2, Swamp) are legal targets for at least one of them. The defensible claim is narrower — Kodama is the only card that finds a basic WITHOUT spending a land drop, a life and the land itself, and off a combat trigger. The error runs conservative (it overstates the cost of a cut the entry grades `easy`), so it pushes no bad swap, but it is a false superlative in the field the pilot reads to decide whether the cut hurts. Everything else in this entry checks out: card_roles gives Kodama ramp:land / threat:body / tutor:narrow, the tutors axis does fall 2 -> 1 under the swap set (recomputed), and the trample claim is exact — 'trample' appears on exactly four cards in the 99 (Kenrith, Kodama, Najeela, Surrak).

Cosmetic but wrong, and in a graded axis's reading: "The permanent taxes (Drannith Magistrate, Grand Abolisher, Kutzil, Thalia, Silence, Teferi) carry the rest of the interactive suite". Silence is an Instant ('Your opponents can't cast spells this turn.') — a one-shot, not a permanent and not a persistent tax. The other five are permanents and do persist (Thalia here is Thalia, Heretic Cathar, the only Thalia in the 99). The axis verdict `adequate` at 8 does not depend on it, and every other figure in this reading is exact: the audit's eight interaction cards are the eight named, six of them counterspells, with Path to Exile and Boros Charm's 4-damage mode as the two that answer a resolved permanent, and Loran / Teferi / Toxic Deluge correctly placed outside the axis.

THE LOAD-BEARING CLAIM, re-derived end to end. I rebuilt the swapped 99 (cuts: An Offer You Can't Refuse, Kodama of the West Tree, Mikaeus, the Lunarch; adds: Chromatic Lantern, Cryptolith Rite, Beast Within) and ran deck_audit._count_copies with AXIS_ROLES over the whole set at once. Result: interaction 8, protection 7, threat-density 3 — exactly as claimed, no floor broken. The counterfactual is also exact: pairing Beast Within with Boros Charm instead gives interaction 7 / protection 6 / threat-density 2, two floors broken. Cutting Boros Charm alone gives 7/6/2. The re-pairing the doctor performed against my pass-2 finding is arithmetically correct. Underlying roles verified in card_roles.json: Boros Charm protection:self + removal:damage + wincon:combat (hence three axes), Beast Within removal:spot + threat:tokens (one interaction slot, no wincon), Walking Ballista buff:counters + removal:damage + threat:body (moves threat-density by zero — the withdrawal was right), Chromatic Lantern and Cryptolith Rite both ramp:rock + utility:activated (no axis in the three). Both cited quotes are verbatim in strategy:deckbuilding.threat-density and strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite, and I read both sections whole. The withdrawal of the pass-2 'Beast Within covers interaction' claim is made in place rather than deleted.

Mikaeus, the Lunarch re-graded `easy`. CR 107.3g fetched via lookup-rule and the quote is verbatim: 'If a card in any zone other than the stack has an {X} in its mana cost, the value of {X} is treated as 0, even if the value of X is defined somewhere within its text.' Sisay's activation (verified from cards.json) puts a card onto the battlefield and never casts it, Mikaeus is {X}{W} with a base 0/0 body and 'Mikaeus enters with X +1/+1 counters on it', so fetched he enters 0/0 and dies to state-based actions — the re-grade holds. His mana value in the library is 1, so he really is inside the base-power-2 fetch pool. The 'exactly three legendary permanents at mana value 1 or less' claim is exact: over the 33 non-commander legendary permanents in cards.json the mana-value histogram is {0:1, 1:2, 2:7, 3:13, 4:5, 5:5}. Roles buff:counters / threat:body / utility:activated appear in no AXIS_ROLES group, so 'no axis moves' is right, and I confirmed it in the swap run. The real cost — he is one of the five counter sources the engine block uses to argue the thinnest component is mis-declared — is named in the entry rather than hidden.

The DFC trap is handled, not merely invoked. Enumerating cards.json, the mana-value-2-or-less legendary permanents are EXACTLY the ten listed, no more and no fewer. Rona, Herald of Invasion // Rona, Tolarian Obliterator: top-level mana_cost is '', card_faces[0] is '{1}{U}' with colors ['U'], and the aggregated `colors` field reads ['U','B'] — so the front face adds one colour, the aggregate would wrongly say two, and the entry says so verbatim. Kinnan is {G}{U} and does take Sisay 3 -> 5 on a mono-white board; Katilda ({G}{W}), Lotho ({W}{B}) and Saffi ({G}{W}) each do it on a mono-blue board. Flowering of the White Tree's oracle text is quoted verbatim and it gives Sisay +2 power from the anthem regardless of board. The ladder 3/10/23/28/33 reproduces exactly from the histogram under 'mana value less than Sisay's power'. The one imprecision is rhetorical, not factual: Mox Amber's gain is also board-independent (constant +0), so 'board-INDEPENDENT' alone is carried by the following clause classifying every other target's gain as a colour count — the operative and true claim is that Flowering is the only one of the ten with a nonzero floor.

The 36-source target derivation is exact. mana_analysis.pips.B carries earliest_turn 2 and effective_pips 2; manabase.source_targets computes turn = max(earliest_turn, effective_pips, MIN_PLANNING_TURN) with MIN_PLANNING_TURN = 3; I called the functions directly: sources_needed(2,3) = 36 and sources_needed(2,2) = 40, matching the entry's 'turn two would ask for 40'. The other four colours land on sources_needed(1,3) = 22, matching source_targets. per_colour reproduces (B 21/36, R 21/22, U 22/22, W 26/22, G 27/22) and short = {B:15, R:1}. Dauthi Voidwalker is verifiably the only {B}{B} two-drop and Sheoldred ({2}{B}{B}) the only other multi-black card in the 99. All four Karsten quotes are verbatim in strategy:deckbuilding.mana-base.color-sources, which I read whole, including its own 'Read them as a budget, not a table' framing — the section is used as it asks to be used.

The probe rule is honoured in the direction it exists for. deck-audit reports card-advantage UNDER at 7 against a target of 10, and its notes name four uncounted probes (Kenrith, Kutzil, Loran, Teferi). The diagnosis grades the axis `adequate`, names all four, and adds two the probe missed which I verified in cards.json: Jodah, the Unifier ('you may cast that card without paying its mana cost' off a legendary spell) and Dihada's -3 ('Put any number of legendary cards from among them into your hand'). It then says 'Do not spend a slot here', and no add targets the axis. Both cited quotes, including the 'counts of *functions*, not cards' caveat, are verbatim in strategy:deckbuilding.ratios — the same section that ends 'Take the categories, derive the counts from the deck's actual failure modes', which the document quotes elsewhere. The Command Zone numbers are nowhere used as a rule.

Neither single_points_of_failure entry is a named combo half dressed as a defect. Relic of Legends' second ability genuinely carries no {T} on Relic; Selvala's is '{G}, {T}: Add X mana in any combination of colors'; Esika grants only to OTHER legendary creatures; Bloom Tender and Faeburrow Elder are 'for each color among permanents you control'. SPOF 2's quotes are verbatim in stack 002's resolution.final_state.summary ('not a self-contained two-card infinite', 'needs a mana base that can produce {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} every combat and at least five creatures connecting with a player'), checker.verdict is 'pass', and the break-even-on-combat-2 concession is carried in the entry itself.

ADJUDICATION A — a cut that is listed and simultaneously held is coherent here, and it is the right call. Suppressing Boros Charm would hide the deck's weakest card, and a cut list with no `painful` entry has dodged the job; the schema's difficulty vocabulary is closed at {easy, contested, painful} and has no 'hold' value, so prose is the only channel available. The hold is not buried in one field — it is stated three times (cut_candidates[2].cost_of_cutting, open_questions[0], gaps[5]), each time with the same testable lift condition (an add carrying a wincon role AND a removal or counterspell role), and the machine-readable prescription is unambiguous because add_candidates[].natural_cut names An Offer You Can't Refuse, Kodama and Mikaeus and nothing points at Boros Charm. I verified the consequence a mis-applying pilot would suffer: cutting it takes interaction to 7 and threat-density to 2, two floors. Recommendation to the orchestrator, not a defect in this document: the diagnosis schema would benefit from an explicit `held: true` or a fourth difficulty value, so the hold survives a reader who scans `card` and `difficulty`. orphans_stack is [] on all four entries and is correct — none of the four appears in stack 002's scenario board or hand.

ADJUDICATION B — the document states the limitation honestly, and the underlying question is only PARTLY settled by strategy.md, so route it rather than hold it against the document. The reading concedes the count ('On the floor by count'), names the three counted cards as filler, names the real kill as stack 002's loop, and names the exposure ('answering the assembly answers the deck'). gaps[5] says outright that this is the axis the prescription cannot improve, records that all three adds carry no wincon role (verified in card_roles.json), and says naming a finisher needs a candidate_pool.json or a deck-recon pass the deck does not have. That is the honest form. On the routing: strategy:deckbuilding.threat-density, which I read whole, ALREADY says 'cEDH compresses that, its finishers being combos' and gives Eisenherz's layering rule ('overlap pieces, so five cards support four combos') — which is literally this deck's shape, since bracket_report lists four two-card infinites all sharing Najeela, i.e. five cards supporting four combos. So the KB is not silent. But that guidance is explicitly scoped to cEDH and this deck's computed floor is bracket 4 Optimized, which strategy:deckbuilding.power-level distinguishes from 5 cEDH; whether a verified loop discharges Zupke's countable floor at bracket 4 is genuinely unsettled. The open question would be sharper if it named the Eisenherz sentence it has to get past.
